name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog:
Badge/hide/download UI (federation-badge.js) was missing entirely on some installs even when running a genuinely up-to-date plugin version, because the only way it got injected into jellyfin-web was a direct write to index.html on disk - silently failing, with just a warning-level log, on any read-only web-root filesystem (common in some Docker layouts). Added a second, serve-time injection path: a request-pipeline middleware that inserts the same script tag into the index.html response on every request, entirely in memory, with no disk write at all. Works regardless of filesystem permissions and self-heals immediately after a jellyfin-web upgrade replaces index.html, with no restart needed. The original file-write injection is kept as-is (still useful, no downside to leaving it).

Fixed a private-IP leak: this server's own auto-detected public URL (used when accepting/sending friend requests) could end up being a LAN or loopback address if the admin happened to be managing Jellyfin from inside their own network, silently handing a friend an address only reachable on that LAN - this was the root cause of at least one friend's library completely failing to sync. The auto-detected URL is now rejected if it's a literal private/loopback IP, falling back to the existing "set your public URL under Advanced settings" error instead of silently shipping a broken address.

Fixed "Last refresh: 12/31/1" showing instead of "Never" on the status strip and Diagnostics panel before the first sync ever completes.

The restricted-sharing setup ("don't share my whole server") required an admin to separately go create a dedicated Jellyfin user via Dashboard > Users first, with no link or indication of that from the Federation sharing panel itself, and no way to pick up that new user without reloading the whole page - added a direct link to Jellyfin's native Add User page and a "Refresh list" button next to the account picker.

Background startup sync (fires ~5s after server start) is now tied to server shutdown instead of running with an unconditional CancellationToken.None, and treats being canceled during shutdown as expected rather than logging it as an error - was a plausible cause of an ObjectDisposedException: IServiceProvider a user hit after an update, though it may also have been transient.

The "Test" button on a friend's server now also reports the Federation plugin version installed there (or that it's missing/undetected), so a version mismatch between two federated servers is visible immediately instead of only showing up later as a confusing sync failure.

200 tests.
